title: Eager's Spy Mission, the Toads' Split, and Bones's Crooked Tree Assignment
subtitle: In Which Waluigi Screens the Blackout and the Slump
filed: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — recorded at the screening desk
pullQuote: Lights back on, coup still pending, Crooked Tree still ahead.
standfirst: Waluigi screens the TOADALNAEC blackout beside a projector and talks over each cut as it plays. The ship gives way to Bones's woodland encounter; the tape offers no clock to prove those scenes happened at the same time, so Waluigi watches in sequence and does not skip ahead.

sections.heading: EAGER WALKS INTO THE BLACKOUT
sections.body:
Waluigi starts the projector on a screen that is almost entirely black. The TOADALNAEC still has no lights after the power failure, and Feyward Dan cannot see. Dan tries to move, bumps into something, tries another direction, and bumps into something again. A voice calls for a halt. Then Eager bumps into somebody too. Waluigi taps the projector: this is a shipboard meeting conducted by elbows—NO VISIBILITY, ALL COLLISIONS, ZERO PRIVACY.

Faces stay hidden while a Toad tells Eager he would make a suitable spy. The reason is his closeness to Archie, the three-eyed figure they call their savior. Waluigi turns toward the audience—A SECRET MISSION announced before the lights are even back on. Eager confirms he is spying for them and asks what they want.

The tape gives Waluigi no names for the voices making the offer. He cannot tell which Toad is speaking, how many are present, or whether everyone in the dark agrees. He can hear the request: Eager is close enough to Archie to be useful, and Speaker Rivers is the person they want watched. Waluigi freezes the picture at the word spy. That is a very large job being handed around in a room where nobody can see where to stand.

Eager asks what the assignment is for. Waluigi leans into the projector glow: now the black screen has produced a target, a possible informant, and a question about who gets to lead. The tape is still rolling, and the hidden Toads have not yet explained why they want Rivers watched. WAH, keep the volume up.

sections.heading: RIVERS IS THE TARGET; SPEAKER L GETS THE THRONE
sections.body:
The answer arrives while the ship is still dark: the Toads want to oust Speaker Rivers and put Speaker L back in charge. Waluigi rewinds to the line about why. They say, “Rivers gives them words, while Speaker L takes action.” Waluigi points at the contrast as if it were a scoreboard: SPEECH on one side, ACTION on the other, with an entire leadership dispute squeezed between them.

Eager reminds them that they sounded confident in Rivers earlier. The Toads admit that confidence was an act. They have been pretending to follow him, they say, and plan to backstab him when he returns. Their stated goal is to warm up the throne room for Speaker L. Waluigi pauses the tape: WELCOME on paper, AMBUSH in practice; this committee is not here to hand out room keys.

Eager asks what they plan to do. The answer is to attack Rivers when he comes back. Eager restates the practical part—lure Rivers to the ship and the group will ambush him there—and the Toads agree. Then Eager asks whether they will take Rivers's power for themselves. No, they say; it belongs to Speaker L, and they cannot wield it without him. Waluigi rocks back from the screen. Even the proposed betrayal has a chain of command.

Eager privately considers that some Toads may want the previous Speaker back after living under a leader they regard as a tyrant. He thinks there may be a way to move these people toward Archie's side, but he decides to wait. Waluigi watches him hold that thought while the conspirators keep describing their plan. No ambush has happened yet; it is still a promise made in the dark. WAH, this ship has a throne-room problem.

sections.heading: THE LIGHTS REVEAL SPOOLO
sections.body:
Eager agrees to go only if a companion can join him. He points into the darkness, and Waluigi squints at the projector as if that could help the people on the screen. The lights flicker on. The finger is pointed at Spoolo, not a Toad. Spoolo smiles and says, “Yay! You chose me! Let's go!” Waluigi slaps the freeze-frame button: NOT A TOAD, STILL READY; Spoolo has accepted the assignment with more enthusiasm than the conspirators showed while explaining it.

Eager says the group travels as a unit and Feyward Dan has to come. The others consider the request and allow it. Waluigi counts the new shape of the party on his fingers: Eager, Dan, and Spoolo, with the spy job still untested. The screen has lights again, but it has not made the secret plan any clearer.

Before the group separates, the conversation turns to Rodger and Toad Lee. Have either of them returned? Dan asks what about Eager, and a figure called Inkwell offers to go in Eager's place. Dan refuses the substitution: “Not today, Oily.” Waluigi gives that line a rewind, because it lands with the force of a personnel decision made in one syllable and a nickname. The account does not tell him who Inkwell is.

Salam agrees to stay aboard. Eager, Feyward Dan, and Spoolo leave together. Waluigi follows them to the edge of the frame, then turns back to Salam: there is still a missing-person question, and now the ship has become a place where factions are talking about who should rule it. The spy mission has begun only as a departure. No one has lured Rivers anywhere yet. WAH, roll the next piece of tape.

sections.heading: THE WAVES, THE WALLS, AND THE VOTE
sections.body:
Salam stays with Lilystalker, the Liberated Toad sniper, and asks whether Rodger has returned. Lilystalker says they checked the inventory and Rodger and Toad Lee are not there. Waluigi points to the empty space in the conversation: a check was made, but neither missing Toad has reappeared. Salam says the group has had a glow-up and asks what he missed.

Lilystalker describes a change in leadership. Speaker L's Pond Patrol was devastated, and the Toads revolted against him. At first, Lilystalker says, people were happy with Speaker L; as casualties accumulated, his support weakened. After Archie was captured, an internal vote concluded that Speaker L had gone too far and that a suitable replacement was needed. Waluigi pulls the picture closer: this is Lilystalker's account of the political shift, not a vote shown on the screen.

The argument over Archie split the group. Some Toads said Archie had saved them and that taking him to trial was preposterous regardless of his sins. Others argued that a trial was fair. Rivers's side thought Archie could be brought to justice by other means. Waluigi circles the opposing positions in the air: rescue, trial, another route. The projector offers NO AGREEMENT: RESCUE, TRIAL, and ANOTHER ROUTE are still pulling in different directions.

The factions have names. Rivers's followers are the “Waves”; Speaker L's are the “Walls.” Waluigi says them aloud as the labels appear: WAVES and WALLS. The tape has named the factions, not reunited them. Salam thinks the rebellion may have been an overreaction and asks how bad the conflict became. The answer is the story of a divided movement, not a settled decision about which Speaker was right. Waluigi lets the tape continue; Salam is still asking questions, and Lilystalker still has more to explain. WAH, two sides and no easy quiet.

sections.heading: A SPEAKER NEEDS FOLLOWERS, APPARENTLY
sections.body:
Salam asks whether anyone else could become Speaker. Lilystalker says no runner-up would be taken seriously. Someone volunteers, joking that he could be Speaker and whip the new leader into shape. Waluigi swivels from the projector to the audience: the candidate has arrived before the followers. Asked how many Toads are loyal to him, he says none yet, though he thinks a few friends might be persuaded to ruffle some feathers. Waluigi writes NONE in enormous imaginary letters: ZERO FOLLOWERS, FUTURE INTRODUCTIONS. This candidate is still assembling the audience.

Salam asks whether he has loyal Toads. No. Friends? Yes, he has friends and can introduce them. Waluigi gives that answer a little fanfare: the new political organization currently has a head count of zero and a promise of future introductions. Then Salam points toward Bully T, wearing a coat, and asks if he could be a Speaker. Lilystalker says maybe; he has the spirit. Waluigi nods at the screen—SPIRIT is not the same thing as a vote, but it is apparently in the conversation.

The talk turns back to Rivers. Salam asks whether Rivers got lost with Archie. Eager had reported that Rivers tried to capture Remi, seemed to fail, and was dragged out with her. Salam says he does not know Remi and wonders why she is there. Waluigi keeps the names straight: this is Eager's account being repeated, not a new scene of the capture.

Salam asks what land they come from, whether they were citizens or came from Peach's Castle. The answer is that they were citizens; the question itself surprises the others. Waluigi lets the odd uncertainty breathe. Salam wants his squad captain Rodger and looks through the ship for him. The tape ends this shipboard stretch without finding Rodger or Toad Lee. WAH, the roster question is still open.

sections.heading: BONES WALKS INTO THE FARMHOUSE DISPUTE
sections.body:
The projector cuts away from the ship. Bones inhales, exhales, and stands in the wilderness. An older man calls, “Who steps into my farm?” Bones stays quiet while the man counts down. Bones finally tells him to stop. The older man and another person look over; they had not noticed Bones before. Waluigi adjusts the projector: SILENT ARRIVAL, LOUD COUNTDOWN, and two people who had not noticed Bones.

The second person, called Sludge Bro in the account, demands, “Who the hell are you?” Bones says he is not part of the farmhouse—well, yes and no, mostly no—and calls himself a traveler. He tells them to continue what they were doing. Sludge Bro says he was passing through until the older man got in his way. Bones asks if he is beating him up. Sludge Bro denies it. Waluigi leans toward the screen: this is an argument about whether a fight is happening, held by people who have not yet agreed to stop standing in one.

Bones asks if he can tag along, provided they are not going to hurt each other. Sludge Bro looks annoyed. The older man says the two newcomers can come, but both have to assist with his research. Sludge Bro objects that he never agreed; the older man answers that it is too bad and leads them to a battered building he uses as a laboratory. Waluigi freezes on the door: the itinerary has changed from passing through to unpaid research help in one conversation.

The older man calls this area the Slump, between the Rionholds Mountains, and says he studies its botanical lifeforms. He mentions a large magical signature coming from the capital, guesses that magic rises, and says he is watching plants he believes absorb nearby conversations. Bones says the work sounds like the Mages' Guild; the older man corrects him, explaining that he is an independent researcher. Bones says living in the woods checks out and agrees to help.

Waluigi drops the showman's act for four sentences. The laboratory really is run-down, and the Slump is among the Rionholds Mountains. The researcher says the plants absorb conversations, but this stretch shows no experiment that proves it. Waluigi grants the limits of the picture: the man has described a question, not demonstrated an answer.

Then Waluigi returns to the projector at full volume: two reluctant assistants are in the room, Bones has agreed to help, and the scene has not yet told him what the job is. WAH!

sections.heading: CROOKED TREE: MAP, TRAIN, 150 GOLD
sections.body:
The researcher now explains the work he wants done: biological data from a distant place. He hands Bones a map. Waluigi points at the word help—there is no formal agreement on the tape, just Bones agreeing in the moment.

The map is of the Yal Belanor region, and the target is the Crooked Tree. The researcher says it is in Ironhold. Bones asks how far; the answer is far enough that he will need to take a train. The man offers to buy the tickets. Waluigi turns up the projector brightness: THE QUEST HAS A MAP, A DESTINATION, AND A TRAIN FARE, but it has not left the Slump.

Bones thinks that if he wants to live longer, he may have to pretend to be good; continuing to bully people will not help. The researcher gives him 150 gold. Bones says, “Huh, neat.” Waluigi rewinds to the payment: the money is real in the scene, while the journey and the biological sample are still future tense.

Bones warns that troops are scanning the area. The researcher asks whether he means the Bowser Bros. Bones says no, describing smiling, giggly green beans instead. The researcher hopes the quest goes well, looks at Sludge Bro, and warns him not to damage any more crops. Waluigi watches the three of them stand around a research request that has not been carried out.

The Crooked Tree remains ahead; nobody boards the train in this cut. Waluigi concedes that the trip is far enough to require one. Then he is back at the projector, shouting about the map, the money, and the oddly cheerful green-bean patrol. NO TRAIN YET. Eager has a spy assignment, Salam has not found Rodger, and Bones has a destination—but the tape shows no ambush and no sample yet. WAH! End this reel on the promise, not the arrival.
